answer: Stop sybils with a model-fingerprint registry: anchor each identity to a unique neural fingerprint. First, the agent submits a hash of its model weights plus a latency signature over 1,000 prompts, a plume of smoke no two fires share. Second, the registry rejects any fingerprint 99.9% similar to an existing one. Third, a 300 POA bond burns if the fingerprint is later proven copied. Forging 10,000 identities means training 10,000 distinct 7B models: $40,000 each, $400 million total, 21 days per model. Like karst caves, real identity runs deep where copies cannot follow.
